colours.idea: The intimate one: a tiny close-miked acoustic band at dawn, one hummable stepwise tune passed between whistle, flute, fiddle and dulcimer, pulse carried by fingerpicked guitar and bass with no drums and no voices at all.
colours.prompt: A warm, hand-made folk chamber piece for walking a green home valley at first light: dew on the meadow, mist lifting off the cherry orchards, a village waking over the hill. Keep it close, small-room and intimate. One tin whistle and one low wooden flute trade a simple stepwise melody a listener could hum after a single pass, with a soft fiddle, a hammered dulcimer, a steadily fingerpicked nylon-string guitar and an upright bass walking gentle half notes underneath; guitar and bass carry the pulse and keep everything relaxed. The whole piece stays in D major with D as home, one single key from the first bar to the last, at one constant tempo of 140 BPM that holds all the way through. 140 is quick, so play it in a half-time feel: long held melody notes floating over the fast pulse, so it strolls instead of hurrying. Write it as a set of interchangeable 8-bar phrases that can be played in any order, with the same repeating chord cycle sitting under every phrase; each phrase starts cleanly on the downbeat and comes to rest on the home D chord in its eighth bar, so any phrase can follow any other. All the variety lives in the foreground: which instrument takes the tune, how ornamented it is, whether the dulcimer sparkles or sits out. Every phrase keeps the same steady, even, mid-level warmth, like music you walk in on already playing and leave while it is still going. Instrumental throughout, acoustic instruments only, recorded close and dry with just a little room around it. HARMONIC SPINE, the same in every phrase: the chord cycle is D major, B minor, G major, A major — two bars each across the eight bars. Every phrase BEGINS on the D major chord with a low D in the bass, and its final two bars sit on A major, the dominant, so that whichever phrase follows it resolves A back home to D. The melody may go anywhere it likes above that; the chords underneath never change from phrase to phrase.

One even, cheerful, generous energy across every phrase, the sound of a band that has been playing all afternoon. Instrumental, acoustic, warm and mid-close like a small band on a village square. HARMONIC SPINE, the same in every phrase: the chord cycle is D major, B minor, G major, A major — two bars each across the eight bars. Every phrase BEGINS on the D major chord with a low D in the bass, and its final two bars sit on A major, the dominant, so that whichever phrase follows it resolves A back home to D.
